thread:
anya: Heads up — onboarding HeliosX (Gemma fork) to Dedicated. After int4 conversion I see weird divergence on long-context summarization vs Llama3 baseline. Suspect rotary headwise scale mismatch + tokenmap aliasing. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam_k: Can you paste the quant config and tokenizer conversion command?

anya: Sure — conversion pipeline is mostly standard but we applied headwise scale folding. Command: `python convert.py --model heliox --quant int4 --fold-rotary-headwise --tokenmap friendly_remap.json`

ben: Quick question: is the tokenizer mapping preserving unknown-token ids? We had a case where unknowns shifted by +1 and embeddings drifted.

anya: Good point. We run `vocab_remap()` that emits a map; sample entry: `{12345: 54321}` — I validated counts but not headwise alignment.

christine: Can you run a tiny bisect? Compare: 1) no headwise fold, 2) fold without rotary scaling, 3) fold with per-head rotary_scale. Metric: summarization rouge-L and perplexity on 2 long docs.

anya: Ran that. Results:
- no fold: Rouge-L 31.2, PPL 12.8
- fold no-rotary-scale: Rouge-L 30.9, PPL 13.1
- fold per-head rotary_scale: Rouge-L 26.7, PPL 18.9 (huge drop)

ben: Wow. That smells like per-head phase mismatch where certain heads wrap and alias tokens. Did you inspect KV cache similarity on first 64 tokens?

anya: Yes — cosine between Llama3 and HeliosX kvcache for heads 3,7,9 drops to ~0.2 while others ~0.9.

christine: Could be a rotary frequency table ordering issue (head dimension vs global stride). Are you using gemma-style head ordering? Some converters accidentally transpose head/feature dims.

sam_k: Also check rotary sin/cos dtype casting. We saw fp16->fp32 conversions causing subtle phase shifts after quant kernels.

anya: I tried forcing fp32 for sin/cos precompute and bumping kernel precision — no change for the bad heads.

infra-bot: model-convert-job 789 completed (exit 0). Artifact: s3://redwood-testing/heliox/1798765432/conv.tar.gz

ben: Can you dump the rotary angles for a bad head vs a good head and diff them? Example snippet: `np.allclose(angles_bad, angles_good, atol=1e-6)` — if false, we have ordering or stride mismatch.

anya: Dumped and compared — ordering differs. Good heads use stride pattern [0, 2, 4, ...], bad heads look like [0, 4, 8, ...] (double stride). Converter bug?

christine: That would explain aliasing — if phase vector picks every other entry, effective frequency doubles and wraps earlier. Token ids remapped then alias to previous positions.

sam_k: Workaround: when quantizing, disable headwise folding for now and ship a patch for converter to preserve rotary stride. Also add a unit test: compare pre/post angles and kvcache per-head correlation > 0.95 on small random input.

anya: I'll open a PR with fixes + test and run a quick smoke on Dedicated. Patch will: 1) ensure head dim ordering preserved, 2) keep sin/cos fp32 until after quant kernel, 3) add tokenmap sanity check for unknown id stability.

ben: For rollout, add an eval gate — block canary if Rouge-L drops >2.0 or PPL increases >10% vs baseline.

anya: Will do. Posting minimal repro and logs here: s3://redwood-debug/heliox/rotary-stride-dump.tar.gz. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-monitor: canary test triggered for heliox — will report back in ~15m.
